newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IBM aims to become leader in Internet.
newsitem.headline: IBM aims to become leader in Internet.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp (IBM) aims to become a leader in the Internet business, said John Patrick, IBM's vice president of Internet Technology on Thursday.
The company intends to achieve this through a range of products to promote electronic business done through the Internet, said Patrick in an interview with Reuters.

"Our strategy is to help our customers get connected to their customers, to enable them to get engaged in what we call e-business or electronic business," said Patrick who is in Singapore to attend an Internet conference.

"E-business is our game plan. It is the way to reach new constituencies and create new relationships and value for our customers," he said. He estimated there would be 200-500 million Internet users in five years time.
He declined to give an estimate of the revenue expected from the Internet business.
IBM's e-business strategy centres on three core areas that will drive business on the World Wide Web -- content management, commerce and collaboration, Patrick said.
The market value of network computing products and services is expected to grow by US$250 billion between 1996 and 2000.
About 65 percent would be from services and customised solutions and it was in this area that IBM expected continued strong growth, he said.

"The strength that IBM has is to be able to put all the pieces together -- the hardware, the software, the network, the services, the consulting -- because we are involved in all those," said Patrick. "That is what will make IBM stand out as a leader."
IBM recently announced its fourth quarter earnings rose 18 percent to $2 billion or $3.93 a share with revenues from its service business growing 22 percent.
The S. company also unveiled a variety of products aimed at linking businesses to new markets and partners via the web.

Separately, IBM is discussing with some of the big Singapore banks and credit card companies to pilot a credit card payment scheme via the Internet, said Lawrence Wee, IBM Singapore managing director.
